title: Int4 fused-op incompatibility causing serving instability and quality drift
creator: Maya Chen
description: Post-incident follow-up for a production regression observed after rolling out an int4 kernel change that introduced a fused softmax-attention path. Symptoms: intermittent quality drift on customer prompt suites, increased 5xx rate on high-batch routes, and several service crashloop incidents under burst load. This ticket captures timeline, root cause analysis, mitigation steps taken, longer-term fixes, and tracked action items.
timeline: 2025-11-11 02:15 UTC - Canaried runtime-2.3 with int4 fused-op optimizations enabled for 5% of traffic
2025-11-11 09:40 UTC - Alerts: elevated error rate on model-route /v1/generate (p95 latency up, 5xx spikes)
2025-11-11 09:55 UTC - First customer report of generation hallucination / quality regression (internal eval suite deviation +18% perplexity)
2025-11-11 10:20 UTC - Oncall rollback to runtime-2.2 for canary cohort; initial mitigation verified
2025-11-11 14:00 UTC - Full rollback of runtime-2.3 across clusters to eliminate instability
2025-11-12 08:30 UTC - Postmortem triage meeting: assigned investigation owners and data collection tasks
impact_summary: Approximately 4 hours of elevated error rates for 5% traffic (canary), and 1 hour of elevated errors during partial rollback propagation. High-severity customer reports (3 paying customers) noted degraded generation quality for int4-backed variants; no PII exposure. Cost impact minimal but SLA exposure risk high due to increased latency and 5xx.
root_cause: The new int4 fused attention-softmax kernel introduced an optimization that assumes canonical KV cache alignment across fused and unfused codepaths. On models with odd tokenization / variable prompt prefix lengths we hit a race in cache indexing causing stale KV reads for a subset of requests. The result was silent correctness drift (altered token distributions) and, under certain batching/sequence-length permutations, index overruns that triggered memory guard faults leading to process crashes. The regression only manifested when: (a) int4 weight-packing layout enabled, (b) request batching > 8 with mixed sequence lengths, and (c) model-specific attention mask edge-cases were present.
mitigation_taken: Immediate rollback of runtime-2.3 fused-op feature flag in canary and then global rollout
Temporary automatic routing rule: route mixed-batch requests to int8 variant for affected models
Added an emergent alert for sudden KL divergence on internal evaluation prompts to detect silent drifts
Hotfix PR to add bounds-check and alignment verification (merged as hotpatch-41023)
long_term_workplan: 1) Add deterministic unit + integration tests in the quant-harness that cover mixed-batching and uneven prompt lengths across representative models (owner: Rahul, estimate: 4)
2) Implement alignment-contract + assertion layer inside KV cache load/store paths so fused/unfused ABI mismatches fail fast (owner: Lina Park, estimate: 5)
3) Enhance canary rollout gating with automatic quality checks (KL divergence, token-level edit distance to baseline) before increasing traffic (owner: Platform-Release, estimate: 3)
4) Expand continuous regression evals for int4 variants in CI with per-commit smoke on small eval sets (owner: MLOps, estimate: 3)
5) Expose a transparent runtime capability flag in Console allowing customers to pin to int8/int4 variants and view known-compatibility notes (owner: Console UX, estimate: 5)
6) Create a fall-back policy at the router level to auto-fallback degraded routes to a stable variant when drift or crashes are detected (owner: Routing, estimate: 5)
7) Post-deployment: run a 48-hour soak with production-like mixed-sequence workloads and telemetry validation before turning fused paths on for >1% traffic (owner: Release, estimate: 2)
8) Document kernel ABI and packing layout expectations in internal developer handbook (owner: DevDocs, estimate: 2)
